name: Snacks & Pantry
tagline: Crackers, dried fruit, preserved foods, ferments, and small bites from every food culture. The category with the widest gap between marketing and reality.

learn.how_we_evaluate: This is the category where label claims are most frequently misleading. 'Natural', 'artisan', 'traditional', 'wholesome' — these words carry no legal definition in most markets. We evaluate what is actually in the product, where the ingredients come from, and whether the label describes the product honestly. Short ingredient lists and named origins are the strongest positive signals here.
what_to_look_for: Named origin for key ingredients — not just country of manufacture
No added sugar where not needed (many 'savoury' snacks contain sugar)
Honest serving size — not calculated to make nutrition figures look better
red_flags: Long ingredient list with numbers (E-codes) or chemical names
'Natural flavour' or 'natural flavouring' — a legal catch-all for many additives
Health claims ('high in fibre', 'source of protein') on an otherwise poor product
Packaging that implies artisan production without evidence

key_terms.definition: A legal category that can include hundreds of approved compounds extracted from natural sources. The term does not mean the flavour is simple, pure, or from the ingredient it implies.
EU-approved food additives with assigned E-numbers. Not all are concerning — E330 is citric acid, E300 is vitamin C. But a long list of E-numbers often indicates a highly processed product.
